name: NVIDIA T4
disclaimer: Illustrative geometry. Die and GDDR6 package footprints drawn to a common scale (1 unit = 4 mm; estimates where noted). SM grid, Tensor Core/RT Core counts inside one SM, and memory-chip placement are symbolic, not exact layouts.

components.name: PCIe card substrate
components.desc: Low-profile, single-slot PCIe card with a passive heatsink. No GDDR6-to-die interposer: GDDR6 chips wire-bond straight to the substrate next to the TU104 die, the same way a GeForce board is built. No NVLink — this card only talks to the host over PCIe.

components.name: TU104 die
components.desc: A single monolithic Turing die — no multi-die package, no interposer. Holds the SMs, L2, GDDR6 memory controllers, display/video engines and the PCIe interface. Built for inference at low power, not for training at the top of the stack.

specs.label: Die size
specs.value: ~545 mm² (third-party die measurements; not published by NVIDIA)

components.name: L2 cache
components.desc: Shared L2 cache between all SMs and the GDDR6 controllers. Small by later-generation standards — Turing relies on GDDR6 bandwidth and per-SM L1/shared memory more than a huge shared L2.

specs.label: Size
specs.value: 4 MB (TU104; third-party measurement, not stated in NVIDIA's T4 datasheet)

components.name: GDDR6 memory controllers
components.desc: 256-bit GDDR6 PHY across 8 independent 32-bit channels, one per memory chip. No HBM, no interposer: GDDR6 keeps per-GB cost and board complexity down for an inference card that doesn't need HBM-class bandwidth.

components.name: Video encode/decode engines
components.desc: Fixed-function NVENC encoder and NVDEC decoder. T4 was widely deployed for combined video transcode + AI inference (e.g. content moderation, transcoding pipelines), but the encode/decode throughput is modest next to Ada's engines.

components.name: PCIe Gen3 x16
components.desc: Only interconnect on the board: PCIe Gen3 x16 to the host. No NVLink — T4 was built to be deployed one-per-server-slot for inference, not scaled across GPUs.

components.name: SMs
components.desc: 40 Streaming Multiprocessors, each with 64 CUDA cores and 8 second-generation Tensor Cores (320 Tensor Cores total). Click **Open SM** to look inside.

components.name: GDDR6 chips (left bank)
components.desc: 4 of the 8 discrete GDDR6 packages, wire-bonded straight to the substrate next to the die — no TSV stack, no HBM base die, no interposer. Each chip is a 32-bit-wide channel; 8 chips together give the 256-bit bus.

specs.label: Chip count / arrangement
specs.value: 8 chips (4 left, 4 right), 2 GB each; exact package layout not disclosed

components.name: GDDR6 chips (right bank)
components.desc: Second bank of 4 GDDR6 packages, mirroring the left bank.

components.name: L1 data cache / shared memory
components.desc: Unified, configurable L1 data cache and shared memory. Load/store units move operand tiles in directly — Turing has no async copy engine (TMA), so a warp issues ordinary loads to bring data in before the Tensor Cores can use it.

specs.label: Size (per SM)
specs.value: Up to 96 KB, configurable between L1 cache and shared memory

components.name: Tensor Core (2nd gen)
components.desc: 8 second-generation Tensor Cores per SM (2 per processing block x 4 blocks), 320 across the GPU. Add FP16 and new INT8/INT4 modes on top of the 1st-gen FP16-only Tensor Core — the precision range that makes T4 an inference-focused part rather than a training part.

specs.label: Supported precisions
specs.value: FP16, INT8, INT4 (no FP8, no FP4 — those arrive with Ada/Hopper)

specs.label: Peak throughput (whole GPU)
specs.value: 65 TFLOPS FP16, 130 TOPS INT8, 260 TOPS INT4

components.name: RT Core (1st gen)
components.desc: One fixed-function ray-tracing core per SM (40 total) — BVH traversal and ray-triangle/ray-box intersection in hardware. Not part of the Tensor Core inference data path; relevant for rendering workloads that share the same card (T4 was also sold as a virtualization/rendering GPU).

components.name: Register file
components.desc: Per-thread registers, one 64 KB slice per processing block (4 per SM) — Turing accumulates Tensor Core results here; there is no separate tensor-memory like later architectures.

components.name: Warp scheduler + CUDA cores
components.desc: Each of the 4 processing blocks has its own warp scheduler issuing one warp per cycle. Scalar FP32/INT32 CUDA cores run the epilogue: bias, activation, requantization back to INT8/INT4.

steps.text: 1. Weights and activations sit in GDDR6 — T4 has no HBM and no interposer, which keeps the board cheap for a 70 W inference card.
2. The GDDR6 memory controller reads the 256-bit bus at up to 320 GB/s.
3. Data lands in the shared L2 cache between the 40 SMs and the memory controllers.
4. Load/store units pull operand tiles from L2 into the SM's L1/shared memory — Turing has no async-copy engine, so a warp issues ordinary loads.
5. The 2nd-gen Tensor Cores multiply the tiles in FP16, INT8 or INT4 — the precision the model was quantized to for inference.
6. Partial sums accumulate directly in the register file (no separate tensor-memory on Turing). Steps 4-6 repeat along K.

7. Alongside the matmul path, each SM also has a 1st-gen RT Core for ray-triangle intersection — used by rendering/virtualization workloads that can share this same card, not by the inference matmul above.
8. Epilogue: CUDA cores add bias, apply activation, and requantize the result back to INT8/INT4.
9. Results write back through the memory controller to GDDR6.
10. Finished output heads out over PCIe Gen3 x16 to the host — there is no NVLink to another GPU on this card.

summary.value: 40 SMs (cut-down TU104; 2,560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores)
130 TOPS dense (Turing has no structured sparsity)
65 TFLOPS FP16 dense, FP32 accumulate (no BF16 support on Turing)
0.32 TB/s (320 GB/s, 256-bit @ 10 Gbps per Turing whitepaper; T4 datasheet lists 300 GB/s)
Standard organic substrate, PCIe card (no CoWoS/interposer, no HBM to route)

scale.basis: Die ~24.6 x 22.8 mm (545 mm², third-party measurement); GDDR6 package footprint ~4 x 3.6 mm per unit (estimate)
